items.title: Meta raises $15 billion in five-part US bond sale
items.summary: Meta is raising $15 billion through five US-dollar bond tranches to help fund AI infrastructure. Disclosed tranches include $3.25 billion due in 2031 at a 5.85% coupon and $3.25 billion due in 2033 at 6.25%.
items.context: Reuters links the borrowing to data-centre and computing expansion. The stated coupons are contractual interest rates on those tranches, not their market yields or a forecast return.

items.title: AMD forecast eases AI spending fears as data-center sales surge
items.summary: AMD projected fourth-quarter revenue of about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, versus analysts’ $16.23 billion estimate. Third-quarter data-centre revenue rose 97% to $8.55 billion, supporting the stronger outlook.
items.context: Chief executive Lisa Su forecast revenue growth above 80% in 2027, compared with analysts’ 77%. These are forward-looking projections, not achieved sales. Reuters reported an 8% after-hours share gain, a dated observation rather than a live quote.

items.title: Brazil economists raise inflation, rate forecasts after Lula reelection
items.summary: Brazil’s weekly economist survey raised the end-2027 inflation forecast to 4.76% from 4.34% and the end-2027 Selic forecast to 12.50% from 11.75%. The poll followed Lula’s October 25 reelection.
items.context: The end-2026 rate forecast also rose, to 13.50% from 13.25%. These are private-sector expectations collected by the central bank, not an announced interest-rate decision.

items.title: Cboe, Citadel Securities-backed group sues US regulator over single-stock 'perps'
items.summary: The Capital Markets Alliance, backed by Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued to block the CFTC’s authorization of single-stock perpetual futures. The regulator had said properly registered markets could begin offering them.
items.context: These contracts have no expiry date and can involve high leverage. The dispute concerns regulatory authority and investor protections; the lawsuit itself is not a court ruling. The CFTC defended its approach.

items.title: BMW cuts automotive outlook for second time as restructuring deepens
items.summary: BMW cut its 2026 automotive EBIT-margin forecast to between −0.5% and +0.5%, from 1%–3%. It cited extra restructuring costs and faster job cuts as demand in China weakened.
items.context: The company also forecast automotive deliveries falling 5%–9.9%, while keeping automotive free-cash-flow guidance above €2.5 billion. EBIT margin measures operating profitability; the revised forecast is not the final annual result.

items.title: US job openings jump in September; layoffs lowest in 1-1/2 years
items.summary: US job openings rose by 333,000 to 7.523 million in September, above the Reuters consensus of 7.100 million. August was revised to 7.190 million, while hiring increased to 5.402 million.
items.context: The JOLTS report measures vacancies and worker flows, not the monthly payroll total. Reuters described a resilient but low-hiring labour market; the release does not itself announce any Federal Reserve policy change.
